summary: We developed an innovative, wearable mechatronic system distributed across an astronaut's spacesuit to comprehensively monitor all vital and physical body metrics. The device integrates advanced sensors to measure body temperature, heart rate, blood oxygen saturation, body hydration levels, as well as tracking speed, spatial location, and balance, with all results displayed instantly on a compact onboard OLED screen. Addressing NASA's challenge to create a system or tool that helps astronauts monitor their health, our solution provides a practical, embedded mechanism that continuously tracks the astronaut's physical and physiological status directly from within the suit, providing real-time self-awareness. This project is crucial because it proactively safeguards astronauts in harsh extraterrestrial environments, enables early detection of physical fatigue, loss of balance, or health fluctuations, and empowers crew members with immediate data to ensure mission safety and success
details:
Our project is an advanced, wearable mechatronic system distributed across an astronaut's spacesuit for comprehensive, real-time physiological and kinematic monitoring.

What it does & How it works: The system is powered by an ESP32 microcontroller connected to a robust sensor array:

  1. A DHT11 sensor (connected to Pin 4) for body temperature and humidity/hydration tracking.
  2. A MAX30102 pulse oximeter (via I2C) to measure heart rate and blood oxygen saturation (SpO2) using specialized algorithms.
  3. An MPU6050 sensor to precisely track motion, 3-axis acceleration (X, Y, Z), and balance.
  4. An auxiliary pulse sensor (connected to Pin 34).

All real-time metrics are processed and displayed instantly on a 128x64 OLED screen (connected via I2C pins SDA: 21, SCL: 22). Furthermore, a Buzzer (connected to Pin 26) acts as an active alarm system, automatically triggering an audio warning if physiological thresholds are exceeded (e.g., temperature > 38°C, abnormal heart rate, or SpO2 < 92%).

Benefits & Intended Impact: Addressing NASA's challenge, our solution provides an embedded, self-contained mechanism that continuously tracks the astronaut's physical status directly within the suit. The intended impact is to proactively safeguard astronauts in harsh extraterrestrial environments, enable early detection of fatigue or loss of balance, and ensure mission safety and sustainability.

Hardware, Tools, & Libraries Used:

  • Hardware & Microcontroller: ESP32 board, DHT11 sensor, MAX30102 sensor, MPU6050 sensor, analog pulse sensor, 128x64 OLED display, Buzzer, and a dedicated power regulation/battery module.
  • Programming Language & Environment: C++ developed using the Arduino IDE.
  • Libraries Used: Wire.h, DHT sensor library by Adafruit, Adafruit Unified Sensor, Adafruit SSD1306, Adafruit GFX Library, SparkFun MAX3010x Pulse and Proximity Sensor Library, Adafruit_MPU6050, and spo2_algorithm.h.

Creativity & Design Factors: The project features a lightweight, distributed architecture built specifically for spacesuits to ensure non-intrusive wearability. Key factors considered include sensor accuracy under extreme conditions, real-time data readability on the OLED display, instant automated buzzer alerts for health anomalies, and seamless hardware-software integration.
